messages:
support_ryan: Heads-up: acme-inc (private VPC) hit TLS failures after last scheduled cert rotation. Their Java SDK gets `javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException: sun.security.validator.ValidatorException: PKIX path building failed: unable to find valid certification path to requested target` when calling our API. They say they uploaded a full chain via the API. Ping @olivia_oncall and @sam_crypto for triage.

olivia_oncall: Can you paste the output from `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect <customer-vip>:443 -servername <host>` from inside their VPC or from our egress node? We need to see what chain the server is sending. Also, any client stack traces and the upload command they used.

support_ryan: Got an s_client capture they ran from a bastion in their VPC:

```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = api.acme.internal
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.acme.internal
   i:/CN=acme-intermediate
---
---SSL handshake has read 3200 bytes and written 452 bytes
---
```
They only see leaf + intermediate name in the chain listed but verification fails. When I asked for the raw certs the server presented just two PEM blocks: leaf and root (no intermediate PEM present).

acme_ops: We uploaded this via our automation. Command was: `curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/private/upload -F 'pem=@bundle.pem' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'`. The file `bundle.pem` contains three certs (leaf, intermediate, root) — we validated locally with `openssl crl2pkcs7 -nocrl -certfile bundle.pem | openssl pkcs7 -print_certs -text -noout` and it showed 3 certs.

sam_crypto: Two hypotheses: 1) our upload parser normalized the chain and removed what it thought was a duplicate intermediate (bug with CRLF/extra whitespace), resulting in the stored bundle missing the intermediate; 2) an edge/proxy between rotator and customer VIP is trimming the chain on egress (some proxies drop certs > N or mis-handle concatenated PEMs). Need rotator upload logs + the stored bundle in S3/DB.

rotator-bot: Upload event 2026-02-18T13:05:22Z: user=acme_ops, filename=bundle.pem, size=6741 bytes, normalization: true, normalized_cert_count=2, removed_indices=[1], note="PEM parser folded CRLF boundaries, collapsed intermediate as duplicate"

maria_support: I filed infra bug #INF-9242 — parser treats windows CRLF separated certs where `-----END CERTIFICATE-----\r\n-----BEGIN` got concatenated into a single token and the intermediate's begin line was ignored. Workaround for now: re-upload a bundle where you ensure a blank line between certs and LF-only line endings. You can run `awk 'BEGIN{RS="-----END CERTIFICATE-----"} NR>1{print "-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n"$0}' bundle.pem > fixed.pem` to enforce breaks.

acme_ops: We can't easily re-upload via UI; automation calls the API. We tried `curl` above — we can update script if you provide exact command and what content is required.

olivia_oncall: For triage: 1) please fetch the exact stored bundle from our rotator (I asked infra to attach). 2) temporarily add the intermediate cert to your Java truststore as a stop-gap: `keytool -importcert -alias acme-intermediate -file intermediate.pem -keystore /path/to/truststore` (restart your app after). 3) confirm whether OCSP stapling is enabled — some clients fail if OCSP stapling is present but our stapler couldn't reach upstream due to egress rules. OCSP responders often use HTTP/80; check outbound allowlist to ocsp responder URLs.

sam_crypto: Also verify the fingerprint of the intermediate we expect vs the one in their bundle. If our parser removed a cert because it thought it matched root or leaf, fingerprint mismatch will show that. Run: `openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256 -in intermediate.pem`.

acme_ops: We checked outbound rules: firewall only allows 443/HTTPS to our VIPs and port 80 is blocked egress. OCSP responder is `ocsp.acme-ca.com` on port 80. If OCSP stapling is on and our stapler can't reach the responder, some client stacks may reject the connection. We'll open a rule to allow outbound to ocsp.acme-ca.com:80.

support_ryan: Infra attached the stored bundle from the upload: it indeed shows only two PEM blocks (leaf + root) and the intermediate is missing. The rotator-bot log above confirms normalization step removed index 1.

maria_support: I've pushed a hotfix to the parser to preserve PEM boundaries and to treat CRLF consistently; deploy will roll out in ~30m. For customers already affected, two remediation paths: 1) customer re-uploads with enforced LF/blank line separation (preferred) or 2) we re-run normalization job to reconstruct missing certs if we can locate them from the original upload object (we may have the raw bytes in upload-s3; engineering is checking).

acme_ops: We'll open a maintenance window and either add the intermediate to our truststore or re-upload. If you can re-run normalization job, that'd be faster. Please advise when fix is live so we can coordinate.

sam_crypto: I'll follow up on S3 raw object retrieval. If raw upload object has all three certs, we can restore the bundle server-side and trigger a new config push to their edge to serve the full chain. If not, ask customer to `curl` the file back to confirm.

olivia_oncall: Next actions summarized: - infra to confirm raw upload S3 object has three certs (in progress) - parser hotfix deploy (maria) - customer to open outbound 80 to ocsp.acme-ca.com as precaution and prepare re-upload script (acme_ops) - SAM to verify fingerprints. I'll create support ticket S-45281 and attach rotator logs.

support_ryan: Thanks all. acme_ops — if you paste one example of the `bundle.pem` (just the BEGIN/END headers + first 80 chars of base64 of the intermediate) we can validate fingerprints quickly. :thumbsup:

acme_ops: Pasted intermediate header/fragment:
```
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIF...ABCD1234...XYZ
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```
support_ryan: Fingerprint we expect for acme-intermediate (sha256): `D2:4F:3A:11:9C:AA:7B:...:C8` — please confirm once you extract with openssl. Closing loop after infra confirms S3 object.

maria_support: Deploy finished: parser hotfix live. I also kicked a one-off job to re-run normalization against uploads in the last 24h for tenant acme-inc; I'll post results when job completes.

rotator-bot: Re-normalization job for tenant=acme-inc started at 2026-02-18T14:12:01Z, found raw objects: 1/1 with 3 certs present, restored bundle and queued push to edge.

support_ryan: Edge push completed and acme confirmed handshake success from their VPC. Customer also added OCSP allowlist as precaution. Marking this thread resolved — follow-ups in S-45281. :white_check_mark:
